whatItDoes: Turn one scene description into a short stitched video. An LLM breaks the scene into a style guide and an ordered shot list, generates each keyframe, animates it into a clip, and joins the clips. Run it with no input and it shoots the built-in sample as a single real shot.
longDescription: Give it one scene description and it produces a short, multi-shot video with a consistent look. A model (`llm.run`) writes a style guide and breaks the scene into a shot list, then image and video generation turn that plan into clips. Keyframes and clips render one at a time, pausing until a webhook says each is ready, then a merge stitches them into one video. Run it with no input and it shoots the built-in sample; set `dryRun` to see the shot list without generating.
notes:
Click **Use this template** and Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it.

Run it with no input and it shoots the built-in sample scene as one real shot: a single keyframe, one clip, no merge job. Pass your own `scene` for a fuller multi-shot video (`numShots`, default 3, max 6). Set `dryRun: true` to stop after planning and see the shot list without generating any images or video. It renders one keyframe and one clip at a time and picks each up on its own; you don't send any signal. It defaults to Kling 2.1 Pro for the video; pass a different `model` (a Wan or Seedance image-to-video id) to change quality and style.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` and `{ "dryRun": true }` to trace the whole graph, or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.
